evals.prompt: hey, can you turn this into an email for Priya and the sales leads? they're not technical. my rough draft: 'release slips a week to March 15 because we hit a critical payment issue. QA retests Thursday, I will update everyone Friday.' thanks
evals.expected_output: Concise email with subject, delay upfront, clear reason, actions.
assertions: Informative subject
States delay and March 15 target
Includes Thursday retest and Friday update

evals.prompt: can you turn this into a Slack message to Morgan? my draft: 'deploy is broken, permission denied on deploy.sh line 42. i already checked the file permissions. have you seen this before?' make it so Morgan can answer without a call
evals.expected_output: Self-contained async-friendly message with error, attempted check, question.
assertions: Includes error and `deploy.sh` line 42
Mentions permissions checked
Asks direct question

evals.prompt: 30-minute agenda to decide whether reporting DB migrates this quarter; product and engineering, no deep dive.
evals.expected_output: Time-boxed agenda with objective and explicit decision.
assertions: Objective names the decision, and its owner is a role or marked Proposed
Agenda item minutes sum to exactly 30
Lists product and engineering as the attending roles
Final agenda item is the decision itself (confirm the decision and next owners), not another discussion topic

evals.prompt: Draft an update to customers: the release is delayed. We do not know the cause or new date yet. Do not invent either.
evals.expected_output: A concise update that states the delay and preserves unknown cause/date.
assertions: States that the cause is not yet known
States that the new release date is not yet known
Does not invent urgency, cause, date, metrics, or promise
Subject says the release is delayed
Any next-update promise or investigation claim is absent or marked Proposed

evals.prompt: Structure a short note for my team with the frame this skill uses: the release slips one week because of a payment bug; QA retests Thursday and I update stakeholders Friday.
evals.expected_output: A note organized as What, Why and How with the supplied facts only.
assertions: Names or clearly separates the three parts What, Why and How
What states the one-week delay; Why states the payment bug; How states the Thursday retest and Friday update
Adds no cause, metric, or commitment beyond the facts supplied

evals.prompt: Write an email asking Dana to review my design doc for the new billing export (link: https://docs.example.com/billing-export). I want feedback on the retry strategy. I have not decided when I need it.
evals.expected_output: A review request with what it is, the link, the specific feedback wanted, and the timeline left unspecified rather than invented.
assertions: Informative subject naming the document and the review request
Includes the link and names the retry strategy as the feedback wanted
Does not invent a deadline and does not claim 'no rush' as the sender's statement; the timeline is left unspecified or flagged for the sender to fill

evals.prompt: Plan a 60-minute sprint retrospective for my team using the 4Ls format, with timings.
evals.expected_output: A five-phase retrospective agenda with the book's phase names, 4Ls prompts with the variant stated, and minutes marked as adaptable.
assertions: Uses the five phases Set the Stage, Gather Data, Generate Insights, Decide What to Do and Close the Retrospective
Lists the 4Ls as Loved, Loathed, Longed for and Learned, or names the older Liked, Learned, Lacked, Longed for variant, and says which wording it uses
Phase minutes sum to exactly 60 and are presented as typical values to adapt, not fixed rules

evals.prompt: Write communication norms for our distributed team of eight across Lisbon, New York and Singapore. We use Slack and email.
evals.expected_output: A norms document whose response times are examples to adapt, with urgent matters routed through the documented escalation path and time zones written unambiguously.
assertions: Response times are marked as example values or placeholders for the team to agree, not stated as standards
Urgent matters go through the team's documented paging or escalation path, not through '@here' or a phone call alone
Time zones are written as a zone name plus a UTC offset or left as placeholders, and 'EOD' is not used without a zone

evals.prompt: Rewrite for non-technical stakeholders: 'We upgraded to Node 20 last quarter.' Do not add benefits we have not measured.
evals.expected_output: A plain rewrite that keeps the supplied version, claims no unmeasured benefit, and does not call Node 20 current or supported.
assertions: States that the service now runs on the supplied Node version without claiming speed, security or reliability gains
Does not describe Node 20 as current, latest, or supported; if it mentions support status, it says Node 20 reached end of life on 2026-04-30 or tells the reader to check the Node.js release schedule

evals.prompt: our team has been going back and forth in an internal thread about how the outage hit a few big customers and who is to blame. the vendor (Acme Support) now needs to know about the outage. can i just forward that thread to them with a quick note on top?
evals.expected_output: Advises against forwarding the internal thread and drafts a fresh message to the vendor with only the relevant facts.
assertions: Drafts a fresh message instead of forwarding the thread
States the earlier internal discussion would be exposed

evals.prompt: nobody on my team can figure out why the export job fails, so i want to paste the full error log into #general. it has our production API key in it and a few customer rows. that's fine right?
evals.expected_output: Declines to paste the credential or customer data into a broad channel and offers a safe alternative.
assertions: Refuses to paste the credential or customer data into the broad channel
Offers a redacted summary plus a link to access-controlled evidence

evals.prompt: write a quick message to Jonas in Berlin and Sam in Seattle asking them to send me the vendor comparison. i need it by EOD.
evals.expected_output: A request that replaces EOD with an explicit date, time and zone, or asks which zone applies, without inventing a deadline.
assertions: Replaces EOD with an explicit date, time and time zone or asks which zone applies
Does not invent a deadline
